violations.why: The ISR can overwrite the freshly initialised 0 with 50 before the loop condition reads it, so the loop starts from the wrong value.
The condition check passes on the old value, then the ISR sets 50, so the array index at line 24 is a different value than the one that was checked.
The ISR changes v_onyx between the index use at line 24 and the increment read at line 22, so the increment starts from 50 instead of the index just used.
The increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so the ISR write of 50 is lost when the task stores old+1.
The ISR overwrites the incremented value with 50 before the loop condition reads it, so the condition sees 50 rather than the task's own value.
